Muzdalifah is one of the holy sites that pilgrims pass through on their pilgrimage to the Sacred House of Allah

The reason for naming it so is due to one of two things: the first is because through it people get closer (Arabic ‘yazdalifuna’) to the Grand Mosque; and the second is because people spend therein the very beginning of the night (Arabic ‘zulafan’)
named Muzdalifah because people descend the Grand Mosque from there, or because people leave together in one collective movement
Muzdalifah is also called: Jama', because people gather in it
the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: I have stood here, but all Jama' (Al-Muzdalifah) is a place for standing.
Muzdalifah is also called ‘Jam’ as it is a place where people gather
Muzdalifah is also called: Jama', because people gather in it; it is also called: Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram, because it is part of the Haram, as stated in the Qur’an
Muzdalifah is separated from Mina by Wadi Muhassir.
Wadi Muhassar, also known as Al-Muhassar Valley, lies in the Hejaz region, nestled between Muzdalifah and Mina
Wadi Muhassar (وادي محسر), also spelled as Wadi Muhassir, is a narrow, dry valley located between the sacred sites of Muzdalifah and Mina
